# From Reservoir to Rooftop: How City Water Finds Its Way Up

Water is heavy. This single fact—roughly 8.34 pounds per gallon, or about 62.4 pounds per cubic foot—governs everything about how a municipal water system works. When you turn on a faucet on the fortieth floor of an apartment building and water comes out with satisfying force, you're witnessing the end of a carefully engineered chain of pressure management that begins miles away, often at an elevation you'll never see. Let's follow that journey in detail.

## The Fundamental Principle: Elevation as Energy

The core insight of water distribution is that elevation is stored energy. Water at a height has gravitational potential energy, and if you give it a path downhill, it will convert that elevation into pressure. Engineers quantify this in "feet of head": every 2.31 feet of elevation difference produces one pound per square inch (psi) of pressure. This is the master conversion that makes the whole system legible.
